name: Shashwat S
bio: Human rights lawyer and co-founder of Janman People's Foundation. Leads Jan Nyay Abhiyan's litigation before the Patna High Court and district courts, mentors district fellows, and anchors a model of public-spirited, movement-aligned lawyering on gender-based and structural injustice.
qualification: B.A (H) History, Kirori Mal College; LLB, Faculty of Law, University of Delhi

name: Shourya Roy
bio: Social worker and researcher overseeing organisational strategy and programme design. Integrates field insights, documentation and policy thinking into Jan Nyay's gender-justice and access-to-justice work.
qualification: B.A (H) History, Kirori Mal College; MSW, PhD pursuing, Delhi School of Social Work, University of Delhi

name: Priyam Agrawal
bio: Co-founder shaping program strategy and organizational direction.

name: Rajeev Rai
bio: Co-founder advising on strategic legal interventions and program development.

name: Bhavi Gumber
bio: Advising the organization on strategic legal interventions and program development.

name: Mugdha
bio: Leading legal research and strategic litigation initiatives with a commitment to social justice.

name: Prakash Kumar
bio: Senior social work professional heading Jan Nyay's field and community work. Coordinates case intake, home visits and institutional linkages with CWCs, AHTUs, DCPUs, OSCs, police and DLSAs, ensuring litigation is grounded in survivors' psycho-social realities.
qualification: Social Work / Community Practice; MSW, Tata Institute of Social Sciences

name: Roshin Jacob (Sister Anupriya)
bio: Coordinates the District Legal Fellowship Programme. Guides fellows on case strategy, drafting, hearing preparation and case-tracking, and designs learning plans to build a cadre of district-level, public-spirited lawyers.
qualification: BSW, Nirmala Niketan, Mumbai; LLB & LLM, St. Joseph's College, Bangalore University

name: Vivek Raj
bio: Working on policy research and analysis to inform the foundation's legal initiatives.

name: Ashwini Pandey
bio: Works across Seemanchal trial courts on domestic violence, sexual offences and other GBV cases. Handles drafting, hearing notes, OSC/DLSA coordination and supports writ and appellate work as part of a public-spirited, justice-oriented practice.

name: Md Nawaz Hassan
bio: Practicing lawyer in Araria and District Legal Fellow with Jan Nyay Abhiyan. Works on POCSO, rape, gender-based violence, custodial deaths, unjust eviction, police brutality and child-theft matters. Earlier interned with MKSS, Jan Jagran Shakti Sangathan and APCR. Sees law as a tool for social transformation and practices in close dialogue with grassroots struggles.

name: Tausif Raza
bio: Practicing criminal defence advocate at Civil Court, Katihar, specialising in trial advocacy, cross-examination and bail. As a District Legal Fellow, undertakes prison visits, legal aid camps, PLV trainings and pro bono representation in GBV, trafficking, false implication and other human-rights matters, ensuring access to justice for undertrials and survivors from marginalised communities.

name: Sachina K
bio: First-generation lawyer from a remote village in Lakhisarai, Bihar. Former Young Lawyers Fellowship District Consultant with SLIC (HRLN) and Bihar Samvidhan Fellow with Nyaaya (Vidhi). Current work in Patna spans domestic violence, dowry prohibition, POCSO, juvenile justice, housing and labour rights, with a strong focus on legal empowerment of marginalised communities.
qualification: B.Sc and LLB, Tilka Manjhi University, Bhagalpur

name: Mithlesh Kumar
bio: Handles GBV and allied criminal matters in Bhagalpur courts. Supports survivors in filing complaints, seeking protection and compensation, and is trained in rigorous documentation and sensitive client engagement.

name: Pintu Kumar Mehta
bio: Law graduate and social worker from Kishanganj with prior experience as a computer teacher, field executive and NGO supervisor. Focuses on taking legal awareness, free legal aid and information on government schemes to communities otherwise excluded due to economic, social or educational barriers — especially SC/ST, minorities, women and children.

name: Nagmani N
bio: First-generation lawyer from Purnia with over five years' experience in criminal and family law. Previously practised at Civil Court, Patna Sadar and provided pro bono assistance during COVID-19. Counsels survivors of GBV and crimes against minors, supports access to welfare schemes, and balances courtroom advocacy with community-oriented legal service.
qualification: B.A LL.B., Bihar Institute of Law, Patna

name: Nitish Kumar
bio: Resident of Gwasi, a village on the countryside of Purnia town. Has been associated with Janman for over 2 years and works closely with communities in different blocks of Purnia.
